chapter.title: Estimation, Hypothesis Tests and Confidence Procedures

sections.title: Null and alternative hypotheses, tests and error probabilities

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C008 (partial): Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.binomial.most.powerful) not supplied for the explicit two-sided failure. The annex writes the p=3/4 bound and its equality case (annex 260-269). The p=1/4 half, which the conclusion 'no test is most powerful simultaneously against p=1/4 and p=3/4' needs, is only 'the reversed calculation forces a=1,b=0 for its maximum power 3/4' (annex 270-272). The power (3/4)a+(1/4)b, its bound 3/4 under a+b<=1 and the equality case are never written. That is a 'similarly'-type step in place of an owed sub-proof.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C012 (partial): Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.confidence.test.inversion) is incomplete for the measurable converse. The claim that integrating out u 'gives jointly measurable randomized tests' rests on annex 381-390. That passage only outlines a monotone-class argument, lists its stages out of order and verifies none of them. It does not invoke the handbook's proved section-measure lemma (thm:p15-section-measures / thm:p15-tonelli, product-measures.tex 143-181). That lemma is stated for two sigma-finite factor measures, while Lambda x X carries none, so even a citation would need adapting. A sketch counts as partial.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C013 (partial): Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.neyman.interval.construction) is incomplete for the reconstruction S(x)=[l(x),u(x)] cap R. A finite lower endpoint is proved to be in S(x) (annex 439-444). A finite upper endpoint is only 'The same argument puts a finite u in S(x)' (annex 445-446). That step is needed for x in A_t <=> l(x)<=t<=u(x), and hence for the coverage identity and the Proposition I-VII reconstruction. No finite a with l<a<u is chosen and condition (3) is not applied to (a,u) in writing, so the step is 'similarly'.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C016 (partial): Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.binomial.confidence.coverage) is incomplete for 'exactly the inversion of the nonrandomized test' and for the acceptance of the upper root endpoint. The lower-endpoint equivalence is argued (annex 581-592). The upper-endpoint equivalence p>u_n(k) <=> F_{n,p}(k)<d and the k=n case are only 'Similarly ...; for k=n, both are false' (annex 593-600). Neither the strict decrease of F with F_{n,u_n(k)}(k)=d, nor u_n(n)=1 with F_{n,p}(n)=1, is written. The coverage bound (annex 609-621) uses the event {F<d}, so it also rests on this unwritten half.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C017 (partial): Argument / full treatment promised by its declared status (proved=annex:p15.binomial.beta.quantiles) is incomplete for the upper-limit formula u_n(k)=Q_{k+1,n-k}(1-d). It rests on F_{n,p}(k)=1-I_p(k+1,n-k), which the annex gives only as 'Likewise' (annex 690-694). Neither F=1-T_{n,p}(k+1) with the T-identity at index k+1, nor a derivative and initial-value match, is written. Only the lower-tail identity is argued (annex 677-689).
